Ozalj Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ozalj, Croatia

Not demolished. Ozalj, founded in the 13th century and first mentioned in 1244 as a free royal town, was known for a castle built in 1278 and later rebuilt into a palace. This cemetery, on private land, existed until 1941 and was formally registered in 1947, though no Jews remained in the town after WWII; the site fell into neglect, becoming overgrown with dense forest, with only about 10 graves surviving as of a 2019 count. Little is known about Ozalj's Jewish community, which numbered about 12 people at the start of the 20th century.
